title: Transitive × intransitive
titleJp: ドアを開ける・ドアが開く
canDo: I can say both verbs of 9 common pairs, each with its particle: ドアを開ける (someone opens it) × ドアが開く (it opens).
I can tell one event from two angles: ルーカスさんがドアを開けました (someone did it) × ドアが開きました (it happened).
I can describe how things are right now with an intransitive verb + ている: 電気がついています, まどがしまっています.
I can ask for or offer a change with the transitive verb: 電気をけしてください, まどをしめましょうか.
I know the honest tip about the pairs: -su verbs are transitive, -aru verbs are intransitive, and -eru can be either.

blocks.t: Warm-up: say the て-form of 開ける, 開く, 入れる, 入る, 出す, 出る, けす and きえる aloud (every state in this lesson is て-form + いる)
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each word and repeat it twice, always saying the pair together with its particle
Grammar: the 2 points, each with its examples read aloud and one 🔬 comparing the block with を and the block with が
Video (block 6): only the part on transitive and intransitive verbs
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: The て-form of all verb groups (lesson 06-1): every state in this lesson is て-form + いる.
〜ている with its two meanings, action in progress and resulting state (lesson 07-1). Here the second meaning becomes the star.
を as the object particle (lesson 03-2) and が as the subject particle (lesson 08-3): in this lesson the particle and the verb are chosen together.
〜てください (lesson 06-2) and 〜ましょうか (lesson 06-4), to ask for a change or offer to make one.

vocab.en: to open (something) — transitive: ドアを開ける
(something) opens, is open — intransitive: ドアが開く
to close (something) — transitive (kanji: 閉める)
(something) closes, is closed — intransitive (kanji: 閉まる)
to put (something) in — transitive
to go in, to enter; to be inside — intransitive
to take (something) out; to hand in; to send — transitive
to come out, to go out; to leave — intransitive
to turn on (a light, the air conditioner) — transitive
(a light) comes on, is on — intransitive
to turn off; to erase — transitive (kanji: 消す)
(a light) goes off; to disappear — intransitive (kanji: 消える)
to break (something) — transitive
to break, to get broken — intransitive
to drop (something); to lose — transitive (kanji: 落とす)
to fall, to drop — intransitive (kanji: 落ちる)
to start (something) — transitive
(something) starts, begins — intransitive

grammar.title: Transitivity pairs (開ける × 開く)
grammar.gloss: someone does it (を) × it happens (が)
grammar.explanation:
Many Japanese verbs come in **pairs**: two verbs that share a kanji and an idea, but look at the event from different sides.
• **Transitive** verb: **someone does something to a thing**. The thing is the object and takes **を**; the doer, when mentioned, takes が or は. ルーカスさんがドアを開けました = "Lucas opened the door."
• **Intransitive** verb: **the thing changes by itself**, or at least nobody is in the picture. The thing is the subject and takes **が**, and there is no を at all. ドアが開きました = "The door opened."
English often uses one verb for both (I opened the door / the door opened). Japanese uses **two different verbs**, so choosing the verb and choosing the particle is **one single decision**.

**The pairs to know** (transitive with を · intransitive with が):
• 開ける (あける) open · 開く (あく) open
• しめる close · しまる close (kanji: 閉める · 閉まる)
• 入れる put in · 入る (はいる) go in, be inside
• 出す take out, hand in · 出る come out, leave
• つける turn on · つく come on
• けす turn off · きえる go off (kanji: 消す · 消える)
• こわす break · こわれる break, get broken
• おとす drop · おちる fall (kanji: 落とす · 落ちる)
• 始める start · 始まる start, begin

**An honest tip.** There is **no rule that works 100%**: you have to learn each pair. But some patterns help:
• A verb ending in **-su** is almost always the transitive one: 出す, けす, こわす, おとす.
• When one verb of a pair ends in **-aru**, it is usually the intransitive one: しまる, 始まる (their partners しめる, 始める end in -eru).
• But **-eru is not a sign of "transitive"**: 開ける, 入れる, つける are transitive, while 出る, きえる, こわれる, おちる are intransitive. So always learn the pair together with its particle: ドアを開ける · ドアが開く.
• 開く has a second reading, ひらく, which can take を (本を開く, "open a book"). For doors and windows, stick to 開ける (を) and 開く (あく, が).

**Reading the sentence.** In the 🔬, a transitive sentence has an **OBJECT** block (with を) before the PREDICATE; an intransitive one has only a **SUBJECT** block (with が). Read the PREDICATE at the end first, then ask: did someone do it, or did it just happen?
grammar.structure: [person] が [thing] を [transitive verb] · [thing] が [intransitive verb]

examples.jp: ルーカスさんがドアを開けました。
examples.kana: ルーカスさんがドアをあけました。
examples.en: Lucas opened the door. [someone did it: the door takes を]

examples.jp: 夜中に、ドアが開きました。
examples.kana: よなかに、ドアがあきました。
examples.en: In the middle of the night, the door opened. [nobody is in the sentence: the door takes が]

examples.jp: 寒いですね。まどをしめましょうか。
examples.kana: さむいですね。まどをしめましょうか。
examples.romaji: Samui desu ne. Mado o shimemashō ka.
examples.en: It's cold, isn't it? Shall I close the window?

pitfalls: The verb and the particle go together: ドアをあきました ✗ → ドアをあけました ✓ (someone opened it) or ドアがあきました ✓ (it opened).
"The light went off", and nobody did it: 電気がけしました ✗ → 電気がきえました ✓. If someone did it: 田中さんが電気をけしました ✓.
-eru does not mean transitive: おちる, きえる, こわれる and 出る are intransitive. さいふをおちました ✗ → さいふをおとしました ✓ (I dropped my wallet).
The を in 家を出ます (I leave the house) marks the place you go out of, not an object: 出る is still intransitive. To take something out you need 出す: ゴミを出る ✗ → ゴミを出す ✓ (take out the garbage).
howToStudy: Make one flashcard per pair, always with its particle: ドアを開ける ⇄ ドアが開く. Say both halves aloud for all 9 pairs, until you can do it without hesitating.

Tap 🔬 on examples 1 and 2 and compare them. In example 1 there is a SUBJECT (ルーカスさんが, the doer) and an OBJECT block (ドアを) before the PREDICATE. In example 2, ドアが is the SUBJECT and there is no OBJECT at all: the door itself does the "happening".
Mime it: turn off a real light while saying 電気をけします, then look at it and say 電気がきえました. Do the same with a door (開ける / 開く), a window (しめる / しまる) and a bag (入れる / 入る).

grammar.title: Intransitive verb + ている (the resulting state)
grammar.gloss: is open, is on, is broken: the state left by a change
grammar.explanation:
In lesson 07-1 you saw that ている has two jobs: an action **in progress** (食べています, "I'm eating") and a **resulting state** (けっこんしています, "I'm married"). With the **intransitive** verb of a pair, ている almost always means the **resulting state**: the change happened at some point, and its result is still there now.
• ドアが開いています = "The door **is open**." It opened earlier and is still open. It does not mean "the door is opening".
• 電気がついています = "The light is on." 電気がきえています = "The light is off."
• パソコンがこわれています = "The computer is broken."
• さいふがおちています = "There's a wallet (lying) on the floor." [lit. a wallet has fallen]
• かばんに本が入っています = "There's a book in the bag."
This is how Japanese says many English adjectives: open, closed, on, off, broken, inside. English describes the state; Japanese names the change and adds ている.

**Transitive + ている is different: it is an action in progress.** ジョンさんは今、まどを開けています = "John is opening the window right now." So ask: is someone doing it right now (transitive + を), or am I just describing how things are (intransitive + が)?
• Negative: 電気がついていません = "The light isn't on." With まだ: 店はまだ開いていません = "The shop isn't open yet."
• Without ている, the verb tells about the change, not the state: 電気がつきます = "the light comes on / will come on". To describe the light right now, use ている.
• In lesson 21-2 you will meet 〜てある (電気がつけてあります), a state someone left **on purpose**. For now, intransitive + ている is the everyday way to describe a state.
• In the 🔬, this PREDICATE shows as "ongoing / state (～ている)": the engine does not choose between "in progress" and "state". **You** decide, by looking at the verb: the intransitive verb of a pair → a state.
grammar.structure: [thing] が [intransitive verb て-form] います (a state, now) · [person] が [thing] を [transitive verb て-form] います (an action in progress)

examples.jp: 教室の電気がついています。
examples.kana: きょうしつのでんきがついています。
examples.romaji: Kyōshitsu no denki ga tsuite imasu.
examples.en: The lights in the classroom are on. [lit. have come on and still are]

examples.jp: 日曜日なので、ゆうびんきょくはしまっています。
examples.kana: にちようびなので、ゆうびんきょくはしまっています。
examples.romaji: Nichiyōbi na node, yūbinkyoku wa shimatte imasu.
examples.en: It's Sunday, so the post office is closed.

examples.jp: あれ、ろうかにさいふがおちています。
examples.kana: あれ、ろうかにさいふがおちています。
examples.romaji: Are, rōka ni saifu ga ochite imasu.
examples.en: Huh? There's a wallet on the floor in the hallway. [lit. a wallet has fallen in the hallway]

pitfalls: "The door is open": ドアを開けています ✗ (that means someone is opening it) → ドアが開いています ✓.
To describe the state now, you need ている: 今、電気がつきます ✗ → 今、電気がついています ✓ (the light is on).
The state keeps が, never を: 電気をついています ✗ → 電気がついています ✓.
"The light is off": 電気がけしています ✗ → 電気がきえています ✓ (or 電気がついていません ✓).
howToStudy: Look around your room and describe 6 things out loud, exactly as they are now: 電気がついています。まどがしまっています。エアコンがきえています。…

Tap 🔬 on example 1: 教室の is DESCRIBES NEXT (attached to 電気が), 電気が is the SUBJECT and ついています is the PREDICATE, shown as "ongoing / state (～ている)". There is no OBJECT: nobody is doing anything, so it is a state.
Detective in reverse: for each state you described, ask who caused it, with the transitive verb: まどが開いています。→ だれがまどを開けたんですか。

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook, with kanji where you know them and kana for the rest. Before writing each sentence, ask: is someone doing it (を + transitive verb), or is it just happening or just a state (が + intransitive verb)? Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day. If you have the Genki II Workbook, do this lesson's exercises too.

tasks.prompt: Choose the right verb of the pair and write the whole sentence, filling in を or が.

items.q: Tanaka opened the window: 田中さん＿まど＿（開けました／開きました）。

a.jp: 田中さんがまどを開けました。
a.kana: たなかさんがまどをあけました。

items.note: Someone did it → transitive verb, the window takes を.

items.q: The door opened in the middle of the night: 夜中にドア＿（開けました／開きました）。

a.jp: 夜中にドアが開きました。
a.kana: よなかにドアがあきました。

items.note: Nobody is in the sentence → intransitive verb, the door takes が.

items.q: Class starts at nine: 九時に授業＿（始めます／始まります）。

a.jp: 九時に授業が始まります。
a.kana: くじにじゅぎょうがはじまります。

items.q: The teacher started the test: 先生がテスト＿（始めました／始まりました）。

a.jp: 先生がテストを始めました。
a.kana: せんせいがテストをはじめました。

items.q: Please turn off the light: 電気＿（けして／きえて）ください。

a.jp: 電気をけしてください。
a.kana: でんきをけしてください。

items.note: A request is always about doing something → transitive.

items.q: In the earthquake, books fell off the shelf (じしん = earthquake, たな = shelf): じしんで、本＿たなから（おとしました／おちました）。

a.jp: じしんで、本がたなからおちました。
a.kana: じしんで、ほんがたなからおちました。
a.romaji: Jishin de, hon ga tana kara ochimashita.

items.note: Nobody dropped them: they fell → intransitive. Here で marks the cause.

tasks.prompt: Someone did something. Describe the result you can see now, with the intransitive verb + ています.

items.q: だれかがまどを開けました。
エミリーさんが電気をつけました。

a.kana: でんきがついています。

items.q: 弟がパソコンをこわしました。

a.jp: パソコンがこわれています。

items.q: 店の人がドアをしめました。

a.jp: ドアがしまっています。

items.note: しめる → しまる → しまっています. Don't mix it up with しめています (someone is closing it).

items.q: ルーカスさんがかばんにさいふを入れました。

a.jp: かばんにさいふが入っています。
a.kana: かばんにさいふがはいっています。
a.romaji: Kaban ni saifu ga haitte imasu.

items.q: だれかが電気をけしました。

a.kana: でんきがきえています。

tasks.prompt: Translate into Japanese. First decide: a state (intransitive + ている), a change that happened, or something someone does (transitive)?

a.jp: エアコンがついています。
まどを開けてください。
a.kana: まどをあけてください。

items.q: The post office isn't open yet.

a.jp: ゆうびんきょくはまだ開いていません。
a.kana: ゆうびんきょくはまだあいていません。

a.jp: さいふをおとしました。

items.note: You did it (even by accident) → transitive おとす. Lesson 18-2 will add the "oh no" feeling.

items.q: Shall I turn off the light?

a.jp: 電気をけしましょうか。
a.kana: でんきをけしましょうか。

a.jp: 授業はもう始まっています。
a.kana: じゅぎょうはもうはじまっています。

items.note: It started and is still going: intransitive + ている. 授業はもう始まりました (it has started) is also correct.

tasks.prompt: Describe your room (or your workplace) right now in 5–6 sentences: at least 4 states with an intransitive verb + ている (use at least 3 different pairs) and 1 sentence where you change something with the transitive verb. Then read it aloud and record it on your phone.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: 今、私のへやはちょっと寒いです。まどが開いています。エアコンはきえています。でも、電気はついています。かばんに本が入っています。まどをしめて、エアコンをつけます。
a.kana: いま、わたしのへやはちょっとさむいです。まどがあいています。エアコンはきえています。でも、でんきはついています。かばんにほんがはいっています。まどをしめて、エアコンをつけます。
a.romaji: Ima, watashi no heya wa chotto samui desu. Mado ga aite imasu. Eakon wa kiete imasu. Demo, denki wa tsuite imasu. Kaban ni hon ga haitte imasu. Mado o shimete, eakon o tsukemasu.
a.en: My room is a bit cold right now. The window is open. The air conditioner is off. But the light is on. There's a book in my bag. I'll close the window and turn on the air conditioner.

items.note: Check: the states use the intransitive verb + ている with が (or は for contrast, as in エアコンは…、電気は…); what you do yourself uses the transitive verb with を.

practice.what: Play in the N4 areas and hunt for doors, lights, boxes and things falling in the dialogues: 開, しまる, 入る, 出る, つく, おちる… For each one, check the particle before the verb: を → someone does it; が → it happens. Log the session in Immersion → Games and paste one of those lines into 🔬 Anatomy to see whether it has an OBJECT block.

Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🔬 Analyze: paste ルーカスさんがドアを開けました。 and ドアが開きました。 one after the other. Then write and analyze 3 pairs of your own (つける / つく, けす / きえる, 入れる / 入る): each transitive sentence should show an OBJECT, and each intransitive one should not.
Write the description of your room (homework h4) in the Journal and open "Anatomy of what I wrote": each state should show a SUBJECT and a PREDICATE marked "ongoing / state (～ている)", with no OBJECT.
Tap 🔊 on each example and repeat along 3 times. Then say each pair as a two-line mini-story: 電気をけします。— 電気がきえました。
Record a 30-second vending-machine scene (see the culture block), using at least 2 transitive and 2 intransitive verbs: お金を入れます。ボタンをおします。ジュースが出ます。…

culture.title: Vending machines (じどうはんばいき)
culture.body: Japan has **millions of vending machines** (じどうはんばいき, often shortened to じはんき): on street corners, in stations, outside shops and even along quiet country roads. Most sell drinks, and many sell both **cold and hot** ones: a blue label usually means cold (つめたい) and a red one means hot (あたたかい), and in winter there are usually more red labels. Most machines take coins and 1,000-yen bills, and many also take IC transit cards. Some sell other things too, such as ice cream or snacks. Buying from one is a small transitive × intransitive drill: you **put in** the money (お金を入れる) and **press** a button (ボタンをおす), then the drink **drops** (おちる) and **comes out** (出る) at the bottom, and so does your change (おつりが出る).
culture.try: Narrate a purchase out loud, like a sports commentator, alternating the verbs: お金を入れます。ボタンをおします。ジュースがおちます。おつりが出ます。 Then tell it as if it went wrong: お金を入れました。でも、ジュースが出ませんでした。

checklist: I can say both verbs of all 9 pairs with their particles (ドアを開ける / ドアが開く) without looking.
I can tell from the particle before the verb whether the sentence needs the transitive verb (を) or the intransitive one (が).
I can describe the state of a room with an intransitive verb + ている: 電気がついています, まどがしまっています.
I know that ドアを開けています is "someone is opening the door" and ドアが開いています is "the door is open".
I can ask for a change with the transitive verb + てください: 電気をけしてください.
I know the honest tip: -su is transitive, -aru is intransitive, -eru can be either, so I learn each pair with its particle.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
If I have the Genki II Workbook, I did the Lesson 18 exercises on transitivity pairs and intransitive verbs + ている.
